note: City of Luling, Caldwell County, TX. INSTRUMENT: Code of Ordinances, Appendix B - Zoning, as currently published on Municode Library. Editor's note at the head of Appendix B reads: "Ord. No. 2013-O-04, adopted March 14, 2013, repealed former App. B, §§ 1.0-10.015, and enacted a new App. B as set out herein. Former App. B pertained to the same subject matter and derived from Ord. No. 2010-O-11, adopted Oct. 14, 2010." effectiveDate is that adoption date, read at source. VINTAGE CAVEAT: the Municode supplement level could not be read at source -- Luling's Municode route is a JavaScript SPA that returns only the app shell to a plain fetch (verified again 2026-09-16: both /codes/code_of_ordinances and the nodeId route return the SPA bootstrap with no ordinance text), so the currency statement Municode normally prints on the landing page was not readable. The Appendix B text coded here is the version Municode currently publishes; treat the 2013-03-14 date as the adoption of the enacted text, not as proof that no later amendment exists. ROUTE (cite the route, not only the URL): the Appendix B text was read from a full-text render of the Municode chapter (6,305 lines captured to a local render artifact during this lane's research), not from a plain HTTP fetch of the citation_url. A plain fetch of the citation_url returns the SPA shell and NO ordinance text -- confirmed on 2026-09-16. Anyone reproducing these quotes must render the Municode page in a browser (or use Municode's own print/download action) first. MODELING. (1) Two sources inside the same ordinance are used: (a) the codified summary 'Table 1' at the head of Appendix B, quoted as the raw table row, and (b) the district regulation sections 3.01-3.13 ('Appendix B, Sec. 3.0x'), quoted as the operative clause. Where they agree the section clause is coded. (2) Where a district states a base value plus a conditional exception (e.g. C-2's rear yard being 0 generally but 25 ft where the lot adjoins a residential district), the GENERAL case is coded and the exception is preserved verbatim in that field's quote. (3) Heights: Luling states height as 'stories or feet' ('No building shall exceed two and one-half (2-1/2) stories or thirty-five (35) feet'), so unlike the Belton/Taylor convention no stories-to-feet conversion problem exists here and the real feet figure is coded. (4) Lot coverage: for A-OS, R-1, RLD, RMD, MH, C-1, C-2, C-3, D and I the coverage clause itself reads 'including impervious surfaces' / 'all impervious surface areas', so max_impervious_pct is coded at the same figure as max_lot_coverage_pct with the same clause quoted -- the ordinance does not state a separate impervious cap distinct from lot coverage. (5) Corner lots: Luling's corner-side provisions are inconsistent across districts -- R-1, RLD and MH state a corner-side yard ONLY for accessory buildings (15 ft back-to-back / 25 ft otherwise) and are silent for the dwelling, so side_corner_ft is coded not_specified there (value mirrors the district's interior side yard) rather than asserting the accessory figure for the dwelling; RMD and RHD DO state the corner side yard for dwellings (10 ft back-to-back / 15 ft otherwise) and 15 ft (the general case) is coded; C-1, C-2, C-3 state 25 ft from an intersecting street. CONFLICTS FOUND AND FLAGGED, NOT SILENTLY RESOLVED. (a) C-3: Table 1 reads Front 50' / Rear 10' / Side 25' while Sec. 3.09(E) reads front 50 ft, side 10 ft, rear 25 ft -- an apparent column transposition between the summary table and the operative section. The section text is coded; where the two disagree the more restrictive of the pair is also the section value in both fields here. (b) MH lot coverage: Table 1 codes MH at 40% while Sec. 3.06(F)(1) states 55% (the same clause RLD carries at 55%, which Table 1 also reports as 55% for RLD). 40% (the more restrictive figure, and the one the ordinance's own summary table states for this district) is coded at reduced confidence 0.6 with both readings preserved in the quote -- flagged for planner review. (c) RHD lot coverage: Table 1 defers ('See Section 3.05 F') and Sec. 3.05(F) contains no lot-coverage cap at all -- its subsections are a per-unit lot-area schedule and a 30% minimum livability open space. max_lot_coverage_pct is coded not_specified rather than inferred. COVERAGE OF THE LIVE GIS VOCABULARY. Luling parcels in the P-255 census carry these district stamps: R-1 (1777), C-2 (225), RLD (221), MH (151), C-3 (104), PD-LADERA (99), P & I (97), RMD (71), C-1 (61), I (42), A-OS (31), EX-AG (6), RHD (2), plus 11 unstamped. All 12 Euclidean districts in Appendix B are coded here (A-OS, R-1, RLD, RMD, RHD, MH, C-1, C-2, C-3, D, I, P&I) -- D has no parcels in the census but is defined in force, so a row exists rather than a future false absence. NOT CODED: PD-LADERA (99 parcels) is a Planned Development district whose standards are set by its own ordinance, not by a district schedule -- routes to the PUD refusal; H is the Historic Overlay District (Sec. 3.12), an overlay on a base district with no independent dimensional schedule, and Table 1 marks every H column 'Reserve'; EX-AG (6 parcels) is NOT a district anywhere in the in-force Appendix B (the district list in Sec. 3.0 and Table 1 do not contain it) -- it is a retired or out-of-city stamp and is neither coded nor guessed at; P&I is coded with every dimensional field not_specified because the ordinance genuinely reserves them (see that row's quotes). SENTINELS: not_specified fields carry 100, the Belton/ldt fan-out convention for a non-binding sentinel, EXCEPT max_height_ft, which carries 999 because the corpus acceptance gate makes 999 the canonical max_height_ft sentinel and BLOCKS on any other value (rule G7, gate.ts:70 and gate.ts:312). No value in this table is a converted or interpolated number.
